This is an appeal under Section 173 (2) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred feeling aggrieved by the award dated 04-10-2016 in Claim Case No. 32/15 by the First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rewa.

entities.text: First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rewa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Facts in brief are that one Santosh Sen aged about 25 years occupation-Hair Cutting Saloon R/o - village Dihia District-Rewa died due to motor vehicle accident on 08-07-2012 that occurred between Mahindra Max Jeep No. MP-17-TA-0556 and MP-17HH-1127.
At the time of accident, Santosh was driving Mahindra Max Jeep No. MP-17-TA-0556 and MP-17HH- 1127 was driven by Raghvendra Singh- Respondent No. 1 and the registered owner was respondent No.2.

The claim was filed by wife of Santosh Singh, mother-Shanti Singh, Father-Budhasen and wife-Smt. Seema Sen and children- Nidhi Sen, Shravan Kumar and Prashant Sen claiming monthly income of Santosh to be Rs.
12,000/- per month.
3. The respondents contested the claim petition.

4. Learned Tribunal framed issues and awarded claim of Rs. 7, 42,000/- as below:-
(a) Loss of Dependency- Rs. 4,000/-x12 =Rs. 48,000/
-1/4=Rs. 36,000/-x17= Rs. 6,12,000/-.
(b) Loss of consortium ( only to wife) = Rs. 1,00,000/-
Buddhsen Sen vs Raghvendra Singh on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76441509/
2 (c) Funeral expenses and non-pecuniary = Rs. 30,000/-
damages -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Total = Rs. 7, 42,000/-
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Feeling aggrieved by the award, this appeal has been preferred for enhancement of Rs. 2,50,000/-
submitting that the monthly income has not been properly appreciated and other heads also have not been considered.
Rate of interest is on the lower side.
6. Perused the order of the Tribunal.
7. Income is on the lower side.
Increase of future prospect has not been considered by the Tribunal.
So, compensation in the head of loss of dependency has to be enhanced.
Rs. 1,40,000/- has to be enhanced only in the head of loss of consortium.

So, this appeal is allowed to full extent and additional amount of Rs. 2,50,000/- be paid by the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 jointly and severally with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of this claim petition i.e. 27-09-2012.
The conditions of disbursement shall be same as per award of the Tribunal.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE PG Buddhsen Sen vs Raghvendra Singh on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76441509/
